title: Rosalind and the Vow
premise: Marine biologist Astrid Dravenmoor has built her life on control: measurable data, contained feelings, and a vow never to repeat the heartbreak that derailed her mother's career. When her research institute launches an anonymous pen-pal program meant to ease staff isolation, she's paired not with a stranger but with Julian Voss, the ambitious grant director whose budget cuts nearly ended her turtle conservation project. Writing under pseudonyms, they confess fears neither would say aloud, falling for each other on paper even as their real-world rivalry sharpens. When identities are revealed at the institute's anniversary gala, Astrid must choose between a prestigious post abroad and the man who has learned to see past her armor; she chooses both, renegotiating her contract to lead a joint coastal sanctuary, proving love and duty can share one shore.
about_author: Coral Yarrow is the pen name of a former science communicator who spent three field seasons on coastal research stations before turning to fiction. She writes romances about people who mistake discipline for safety, drawing on salt air, tide charts, and second chances.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. On the survey boat, Astrid logs nesting data and deflects her assistant's questions about why she never dates, revealing the vow she made after her mother's ruinous love affair. Emotional beat: controlled solitude established as armor.

chapters.title: The Memo
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Grant director Julian Voss announces budget cuts that gut Astrid's project, then signs off on the institute's new anonymous pen-pal wellness program as an HR box to tick. Emotional beat: his pragmatism masks loneliness he won't name.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A database glitch pairs 'Tidecaller' (Astrid) with 'Driftwood' (Julian), though neither knows it. Their first letters are stiff, almost hostile, each recognizing the other's institutional jargon. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity kindles.

chapters.title: Salt and Paper
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Letters grow honest: Tidecaller admits fear of becoming her mother; Driftwood confesses he chose administration because he failed as a field scientist. In person, they argue over funding. Emotional beat: intimacy blooming in anonymity.

chapters.title: Low Tide
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A storm strands hatchlings; Julian unexpectedly shows up to help shovel sandbags, working beside her in silence until dawn. Neither mentions it in their next letters. Emotional beat: first crack in mutual contempt.

chapters.title: What Driftwood Knows
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Reviewing pen-pal metadata to justify the program's budget, Julian realizes Tidecaller is Astrid—and says nothing, ashamed of how much he wants the letters to continue. Emotional beat: guilty knowledge, deepening attachment.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid is offered a dream post leading a marine institute in Norway—starting in eight weeks. She writes to Driftwood about a choice she can't explain, asking what loyalty to a place really means. Emotional beat: stakes crystallize.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian's rival colleague suspects the pen-pal pairing was tampered with and threatens to expose the glitch, which could end the program and Julian's career. Julian begins steering Astrid away from the truth. Emotional beat: secrecy curdles into deception.

chapters.title: Nesting Season
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. During a night patrol, Astrid and Julian share whiskey on the dunes and an almost-kiss interrupted by a radio call. Both retreat; both write feverish letters that night. Emotional beat: desire outpacing denial.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Astrid realizes she's falling for two versions of one man—the ally in letters, the adversary in meetings—and hates herself for it. Julian drafts a confession email a dozen times and deletes each. Emotional beat: the lie becomes unbearable.

chapters.title: The Rival Moves
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. The colleague leaks the pairing glitch to HR; Julian is suspended pending investigation, and the pen-pal archive is seized—including everything Tidecaller wrote him. Emotional beat: protective panic; he'd rather lose everything than expose her.

chapters.title: Silence Between Tides
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Driftwood stops writing. Astrid, interpreting it as abandonment, accepts the Norway post and begins packing, hardening the vow around her heart again. Emotional beat: heartbreak rehearsed, armor reforged.

chapters.title: Archive
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Facing termination, Julian bargains to keep the letters sealed by claiming sole authorship of both sides—a fabrication his rival gleefully dismantles. Astrid is summoned to review 'her' confiscated letters. Emotional beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: Revelation
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Reading her own words in the evidence file, Astrid recognizes the handwriting appended beneath them: Driftwood is Julian. Fury and grief collide—every kindness reframed as manipulation. Emotional beat: betrayal at its sharpest.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Seawall
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Astrid confronts Julian in a rainstorm; he admits when he learned the truth and why he stayed silent—not to deceive her but because he loved being known. She walks away anyway. Emotional beat: love declared too late.

chapters.title: Hatchlings
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. On her last night of fieldwork, Astrid watches hatchlings scramble toward a light they trust blindly, and understands her vow protected nothing—it only kept her from choosing. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed; duty redefined.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. At the disciplinary hearing, Julian refuses to blame the glitch or Astrid, taking full responsibility and resigning. His integrity costs him the career he built to hide behind. Emotional beat: sacrifice without expectation.

chapters.title: Departure Board
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the airport, Astrid reads a final letter slipped into her luggage—Driftwood's goodbye, giving her permission to go and meaning every word. She boards, then doesn't. Emotional beat: the choice made freely, not from fear.

chapters.title: Anniversary Gala
chapters.summary: Both POVs. At the institute gala, Astrid returns unannounced, presenting a proposal for a jointly funded coastal sanctuary with Julian's name on it. Before the crowd, she reveals she was Tidecaller all along. Emotional beat: public vulnerability, private courage.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returns
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian, unemployed and unarmored, meets Astrid on the beach where they fought the storm. No pseudonyms, no vows—just names spoken aloud for the first time as true ones. Emotional beat: reunion stripped of pretense.

chapters.title: The New Vow
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Weeks later, Astrid leads the sanctuary's first season with Julian as her co-director, rewriting her old vow into something livable: not a closed heart, but a chosen one. Emotional beat: belonging earned, identity whole.

chapters.title: Epilogue: First Light
chapters.summary: Shared POV. One year on, the couple finds a letter washed in a bottle—an old pen-pal note neither sent—and laugh, adding their own before releasing it to the sea. Final image: two sets of footprints below the high-tide line. Emotional beat: quiet, durable joy.
